headline_finding.one_line: The canonical full-suite coverage command yields 65.59% and PASSES the 40% gate. The 36.63% figure reported by M9-C42.18 was produced by running only tests/unit/engines/ (843 tests) while labelling it the canonical full-suite command. There is no genuine coverage gate failure.
headline_finding.pytest_cov_verbatim: Required test coverage of 40.0% reached. Total coverage: 65.59%

engine_subset_reproduction_of_m9_c42_18.pytest_cov_verbatim: FAIL Required test coverage of 40.0% not reached. Total coverage: 36.63%

two_measurements_reconciled.why_identical_statement_population: Both runs measure the SAME 10,238 statements under the SAME .coveragerc. Only the executing test population differs. This proves the discrepancy is a TEST-SCOPE difference, not a coverage-configuration difference.
two_measurements_reconciled.m9_c42_18_self_inconsistency: M9-C42.18 recorded canonical_command as '... tests/' but its own coverage_baseline.command field records '... tests/unit/engines/'. Additionally its own numbers 3916/10238 = 38.25%, not the 36.63% it reported (36.63% is the branch-inclusive figure), so its coverage narrative was internally inconsistent.

source_area_contribution.note: Actual repository data from the canonical full-suite run. Categories derived from real paths under backend/src; none fabricated. Percentages are line-based per area; the 65.59% total is branch-inclusive.

engines_other.composition: financial_intelligence (807 stmts, 34.82%), transaction_intelligence (367 stmts, 24.25%), financial_events (184 stmts, 90.22%), recommendation_engine (73 stmts, 95.89%), ledger_audit_engine (46 stmts, 93.48%), engines/__init__ (2 stmts, 100%)

gap_attribution.question: Which source areas were responsible for the apparent 36.63% aggregate?
gap_attribution.answer: Areas that NO engine unit test exercises. Under the engine-only subset these measured 0% or near-0%; under the full suite they are well covered by capability, property, contract, golden, and domain tests that the subset excluded.

p0_engines_all_well_covered.conclusion: All four engines in the mutation campaign are at 93-99% line coverage. The coverage gap is NOT in the campaign's engines.

question_1_why_40.answer: It was deliberately calibrated DOWN from 60 to 40 to match a then-realistic measured baseline after excluding untestable modules.
question_1_why_40.origin_subject: feat(coverage): reset threshold to 40% with exclusions + 189 new unit tests
verbatim_commit_evidence: Set fail_under=40 (was 60) to match realistic baseline
Updated .coveragerc to exclude untestable modules (extraction pipeline, entry points, routers) from unit coverage measurement
Updated check_coverage_threshold.py thresholds: overall=40, engines=70, repositories=40, services=40
Overall coverage: 49.2% (up from 31.15%), all 4 threshold groups pass
question_1_why_40.first_introduced_fail_under: f0e732e8 (feat: complete Phase 0 CI integration and workflow fixes)

question_2_backend_wide.answer: YES for the measured SOURCE population (source = src, minus documented omits). The threshold is an aggregate over all of backend/src, not an engine-only threshold.
question_2_backend_wide.evidence: .coveragerc [run] source = src with an omit list; [report] fail_under = 40 applies to the aggregate total.

question_3_engine_code_only.answer: NO. Engine code has a SEPARATE and HIGHER intended threshold of 70%.
question_3_engine_code_only.implication: The 40% figure was never intended as an engine-code threshold. Applying 40% to an engine-only test subset (as M9-C42.18 did) mismatches the threshold to a population it was not designed for.

question_4_legacy.answer: PARTIALLY LEGACY. It is a deliberately-set Phase 1 value explicitly annotated as temporary.
question_4_legacy.evidence: check_coverage_threshold.py comments: '# Phase 1 thresholds (current)', 'overall: 40,  # Will increase in Phase 2', 'repositories: 40,  # Will increase in Phase 2'.
question_4_legacy.note: The measured full-suite coverage is now 65.59%, well above the Phase-1 value of 40%, indicating the threshold now lags actual quality.

question_5_enforced_by_pytest.mechanism: fail_under = 40 in .coveragerc [report]; pytest-cov reads --cov-config=.coveragerc and fails the run. Observed verbatim: 'FAIL Required test coverage of 40.0% not reached' (subset) and 'Required test coverage of 40.0% reached' (full suite).

question_6_enforced_by_ci.answer: NO backend coverage gate was found in CI.
question_6_enforced_by_ci.evidence: No --cov or .coveragerc invocation exists in any of the 13 .github/workflows/*.yml files. backend/pyproject.toml contains NO coverage settings. .github/scripts/check_coverage_threshold.py still exists but is not wired into any workflow, and an earlier M9 artifact (m9-c42.11) already classified it 'D (redundant) — coverage checked by .coveragerc'.
question_6_enforced_by_ci.consequence: The 40% gate is effectively a LOCAL/advisory gate that binds only when a developer or a phase script explicitly passes --cov with --cov-config=.coveragerc.

question_7_advisory.answer: YES in CI (not enforced there); BINDING locally whenever --cov + --cov-config=.coveragerc are used.

question_8_scope_match.answer: NO — not as M9-C42.18 applied it.
question_8_scope_match.detail: The threshold was calibrated against a broad unit-test population (823 unit tests across money/calculations/formatting/parsing/errors and more) measured over all of src. M9-C42.18 applied it to tests/unit/engines/ only (843 tests confined to engine directories), which structurally cannot execute services/, common/, orchestration/, or cashflow code paths. The canonical full-suite command DOES cover the intended source population and yields 65.59% (PASS).
question_8_scope_match.verdict: The 40% threshold is CORRECTLY CALIBRATED for the intended population; it was INCORRECTLY APPLIED to an engine-only test subset in M9-C42.18.

recommendation.rationale: The threshold is not the problem. The measurement scope was. The canonical full-suite command already passes at 65.59%. Changing the threshold would be unjustified in either direction and is explicitly forbidden this phase.
recommendation.smallest_correct_action: Fix the MEASUREMENT COMMAND OF RECORD, not the threshold. Any phase that cites the 40% gate must run the full tests/ suite (the population the threshold was designed for) and must not substitute tests/unit/engines/.
recommendation.optional_future_consideration: Because measured full-suite coverage (65.59%) now far exceeds the Phase-1 value of 40%, a future phase may wish to raise the threshold in line with the 'Will increase in Phase 2' annotation. That is OUT OF SCOPE here and no change was made.
